news.title: Gianni Infantino: Fifa president indicates there could a greater cash pledge to members
news.lede: Gianni Infantino was first elected as Fifa president in 2016. Gianni Infantino has indicated a greater amount of money could be distributed to Fifa members from its estimated £4.4bn cash reserves. In a letter seen by BBC Sport, and sent to the governing body's six continental confederations on Monday, Fifa president Infantino said he would support "the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered". Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which proposed selling stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, sparking a major backlash.

news.title: Lewis Hall using World Cup disappointment as motivation after England recall
news.lede: Lewis Hall has revealed that he is using the disappointment of missing the World Cup to fuel his attempt to establish himself in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad. The Newcastle United defender was overlooked for the tournament in the United States, Canada and Mexico, where England eventually finished third after beating France in the bronze-medal match. Hall has responded impressively at club level and was recalled by Tuchel for England’s opening Nations League fixtures of the new campaign. The 22-year-old admitted his World Cup omission hurt but believes channelling that frustration positively can help him force his way into Tuchel’s long-term plans.

news.title: Europe’s top-flight clubs to get share of £185m from Club World Cup
news.lede: Europe dividing money 50-50 with rest of the world. Confirmation expected after Fifa meeting in October. Europe’s top-flight clubs will share half of the $250m (£185m) solidarity pot from the Club World Cup last year, ending a saga that had caused widespread frustration among those who did not participate in the tournament. Fifa and European Football Clubs (EFC) are close to an agreement that would bring a 50-50 split between sides in Europe and the rest of the world.

news.title: Lewis Hall using World Cup snub as fuel to win England boss Thomas Tuchel over
news.lede: Lewis Hall says he is using the pain of World Cup rejection as fuel this season. The Newcastle left-back has started the campaign in great form for his club and that earned him an instant recall from Thomas Tuchel after he missed out in the summer. Hall has signed a new deal at Newcastle , looks in great shape and wants to make the England left-back slot his own. When asked whether the World Cup heartbreak as fuel, Hall said: “Yeah, I think it's important to use that.

news.title: Ruud Gullit says South Africa and emerging nations have closed the gap on football's elite
news.lede: Dutch legend Ruud Gullit praised Bafana Bafana's historic World Cup run, highlighting how rising physical conditioning and defensive structure across smaller nations are making international football tougher for established powerhouses like France and Spain.
